articles.title: How 'Book Queen' Dolly Parton inspired millions of children with gift of reading
articles.summary: Families across the globe share how free books from Parton's Imagination Library helped their children.
articles.content:
One child in Denver called her "The Book Queen".

Another in Alabama calls her "Ms Dolly".

Across the globe in Australia, a toddler with speech delays delighted her family with her first word - "orange" - after she and her twin sister received a free book in the post about colours. It came from Imagination Library, the literacy programme begun by late global superstar Dolly Parton.

Parton, who died this week aged 80, launched the philanthropic effort in 1995 to honour her father - whose difficult Appalachian upbringing never allowed him to finish school or learn to read and write.

"He was the smartest man I have ever known, but I know in my heart his inability to read probably kept him from fulfilling all of his dreams," wrote Parton in an open letter on Imagination Library's website.

"Inspiring kids to love to read became my mission."
articles.reasoning: The article highlights Dolly Parton's philanthropic literacy program, Imagination Library, which has provided free books to children worldwide, inspiring a love of reading and supporting early childhood development. This has a broad positive impact on families and children's education globally, with clear context and meaningful substance.
articles.personality_title: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library sparks love of reading worldwide
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Dolly Parton, a famous singer and songwriter, started the Imagination Library in 1995. She created it to help children get free books because her own father never learned to read and write.

**What happened** – Since then, the program has sent millions of free books to children around the world. Families from places like the United States and Australia have shared how receiving these books helped their children, including a toddler who said her first word after getting a book about colors.

**Impact** – The program helps children develop reading skills early, which is important for their learning and future success. It also brings joy to families and encourages kids to enjoy books, something that might not happen without this support.

**What's next step** – The Imagination Library will continue to send free books to children, reaching even more families globally. This ongoing effort can help more kids learn to read and discover new worlds through books.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Dolly Parton's Imagination Library has given millions of children free books that inspire a love for reading and help build important skills.
articles.personality_title_fr: La Bibliothèque Imaginaire de Dolly Parton inspire la lecture dans le monde entier
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Dolly Parton, une chanteuse célèbre, a créé la Bibliothèque Imaginaire en 1995. Elle voulait aider les enfants à recevoir des livres gratuits, car son propre père n'avait jamais appris à lire ni à écrire.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Depuis, le programme a envoyé des millions de livres gratuits aux enfants dans le monde entier. Des familles des États-Unis et d'Australie racontent comment ces livres ont aidé leurs enfants, comme une petite fille qui a prononcé son premier mot après avoir reçu un livre sur les couleurs.

**Impact** – Ce programme aide les enfants à apprendre à lire tôt, ce qui est important pour leur apprentissage et leur avenir. Il apporte aussi de la joie aux familles et encourage les enfants à aimer les livres, ce qui ne serait pas toujours possible sans ce soutien.

**Prochaine étape** – La Bibliothèque Imaginaire continuera à envoyer des livres gratuits aux enfants, touchant encore plus de familles dans le monde. Cet effort peut aider davantage d'enfants à apprendre à lire et à découvrir de nouveaux univers grâce aux livres.

**Phrase clé** – La Bibliothèque Imaginaire de Dolly Parton a offert des millions de livres gratuits aux enfants, leur donnant envie de lire et aidant à développer des compétences importantes.
articles.personality_title_es: La Biblioteca de la Imaginación de Dolly Parton impulsa el amor por la lectura en todo el mundo
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Dolly Parton, una cantante famosa, comenzó la Biblioteca de la Imaginación en 1995. Lo hizo para ayudar a los niños a recibir libros gratis, porque su propio padre nunca aprendió a leer ni a escribir.

**Qué pasó** – Desde entonces, el programa ha enviado millones de libros gratuitos a niños de todo el mundo. Familias de Estados Unidos y Australia compartieron cómo los libros ayudaron a sus hijos, como una niña que dijo su primera palabra después de recibir un libro sobre colores.

**Impacto** – El programa ayuda a los niños a aprender a leer desde pequeños, algo muy importante para su educación y futuro. También trae alegría a las familias y anima a los niños a disfrutar de los libros, algo que no siempre pasa sin esta ayuda.

**Próximo paso** – La Biblioteca de la Imaginación seguirá enviando libros gratuitos a más niños y familias en todo el mundo. Este esfuerzo puede ayudar a más niños a aprender a leer y a descubrir nuevos mundos a través de los libros.

**Frase clave** – La Biblioteca de la Imaginación de Dolly Parton ha regalado millones de libros que inspiran a los niños a amar la lectura y a desarrollar habilidades importantes.
